  This is the time set aside for members of the public to address the City Council on
  items of interest that are not on the Agenda, but are within the subject matter

  In an effort to provide everyone with an opportunity to speak tonight, please be

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 15, 2019  2
   A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of September 17, 2019.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of October 1, 2019.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  This is the presentation of the “Register of Demands and Warrants” for the
  payment of City expenditures.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  C. FIRE DEPARTMENT PURCHASE ORDER FOR EMS SUPPLIES AND
  EQUIPMENT

  The San Gabriel Fire Department, in the course of daily operations, maintains a
  supply of expendable items and durable equipment to fulfill its mission. Open
  Purchase Orders are used to keep the department stocked with paramedic and
  firefighting supplies, delivered on an as needed basis. Vendors, reviewed
  regularly, are selected through competitive bid, piggyback and cooperative
  purchasing agreements. In accordance with the updated City of San Gabriel
  (“City”) Purchasing Policy, San Gabriel Municipal Code Section 34.35, Staff
  respectfully requests the San Gabriel City Council authorize the issuance of an
  open purchase order to Life Assist, Inc. in the amount of $65,000, as detailed in
  this report. Life Assist, Inc. is the City’s principal supplier for paramedic supplies
  and equipment. The City of Pasadena, on behalf of the Verdugo Fire Agencies,
  bids and contracts for EMS supplies for the area every two years. Staff has
  determined that it is in the best interest of the City to waive formal bidding and
  piggyback on the terms and pricing offered to the City of Pasadena for EMS
  supplies.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the issuance of an open
  purchase order in the amount of $65,000 to Life Assist, Inc. in accordance to
  the cooperative and piggyback purchasing procedures within Municipal Code
  section 34.35. Funding for this expense is available within account number 121-
  761-00-21-000.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 15, 2019  3
   D. RESOLUTION NO. 19-45 FOR TEMPORARY STREET CLOSURE AT THE
  INTERSECTION OF ADELYN DRIVE AND ROSEMONT BOULEVARD ON
  NOVEMBER 2, 2019

  The Public Works Department received a request from Louis Origel and Bret
  Thompson for a temporary street closure for a neighborhood block party on
  Saturday, November 2, 2019 from 3:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. at the intersection of
  Adelyn Drive and Rosemont Boulevard. The street closure will enable the
  community members to congregate safely in a centralized location. Resolution
  No. 19-45 details the location, date and times for the closure, as well the
  conditions that must be followed by the applicant. The Public Works
  Department (Engineering and Field Operations), Fire Department and Police
  Department have reviewed and approved the request.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-45 authorizing
  closure of the intersection of Adelyn Drive and Rosemont Boulevard from 3:00
  p.m. to 8:00 p.m. on Saturday, November 2, 2019.

  E. RESOLUTION NO. 19-48 FOR TEMPORARY STREET CLOSURE AT 864
  COMMERCIAL AVENUE BETWEEN GLADYS AND THE RUBIO WASH ON
  NOVEMBER 2, 2019

  The Public Works Department received a request from Jacob Gustafson, on
  behalf of the San Gabriel Firefighter’s Association, for a temporary street closure
  for a Fundraiser For Cancer event on Saturday, November 2, 2019 from 5:00
  p.m. to 10:00 p.m. on Commercial Avenue between Gladys Avenue and the
  Rubio Wash. Resolution No. 19-48 details the location, date and times for the
  closure, as well the conditions that must be followed by the applicant. The
  Public Works Department, Fire Department and Police Department have
  reviewed and approved the request.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-48 authorizing
  closure of Commercial Avenue between Gladys Avenue and the Rubio Wash
  from 5:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. on Saturday, November 2, 2019.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 15, 2019  4
   F. ACCEPTANCE OF FINAL PARCEL MAP NO. 72696 (314 E. MISSION ROAD)
  PLANNING CASE PL-41-070

  The development is located at 314 E. Mission Road and is a four-unit
  condominium development on a 17,420 square foot lot. The lot is currently
  developed with an existing 2,337 square feet single family residence
  constructed in 1920. City Staff and the Los Angeles County Department of
  Public Works have reviewed the Final Parcel Map and have determined it is in
  compliance with the State Subdivision Map Act, conditions of approval, and the
  City’s ordinances regarding subdivision.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council accept the Final Parcel Map No. 72696
  and authorize filing with the Los Angeles County Recorder upon the Covenants,
  Conditions, and Restrictions requirement is satisfied.

  G. AUTHORIZATION TO EXECUTE AMENDMENT TO PROFESSIONAL
  SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH IMPRENTA COMMUNICATIONS GROUP IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $35,128, FOR EDUCATION AND OUTREACH SERVICES
  FOR A SALES TAX BALLOT INITIATIVE

  The City of San Gabriel currently has a contract with Imprenta Communications
  Group for education and outreach services for a professional sales tax ballot
  initiative. The original contract anticipated an election occurring in November
  2019. After receiving the results of a potential voter poll, the City Council
  directed staff to look to March of 2020 for the election due to a higher
  likelihood that the ballot initiative could be successful. The proposed
  amendment will increase the contract from $65,372 to $100,500 to allow for a
  more robust education and outreach effort.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  the attached Amendment Number One to the Professional Services Agreement
  with Imprenta Communications Group.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. NEW BUSINESS

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 15, 2019  5
   A. CONSIDERATION OF RESOLUTIONS RELATING TO SAN GABRIEL’S
  GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION TO BE HELD ON MARCH 3, 2020,
  INCLUDING PLACING A MEASURE ENACTING AN ORDINANCE FOR A
  TRANSACTIONS AND USE TAX ON THE MARCH 2020 BALLOT

  This item calls the General Municipal Election for March 3, 2020, for the election
  of two Members of the City Council and a ballot measure to enact a transactions
  and use tax ordinance; requests consolidation of the election with the Statewide
  Primary election of the same date; adopts regulations for candidates’
  statements; directs the City Attorney to prepare an impartial analysis of the
  measure; designates Council Members to prepare and submit a ballot
  argument in favor of the measure; and provides for rebuttal arguments relating
  to the ballot measure.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 19-49 calling for the holding of a General Municipal
  Election on Tuesday, March 3, 2020, ordering that a measure for an
  ordinance enacting a transaction and use sales tax be submitted to the
  voters, directing the City Attorney to prepare an impartial analysis of the
  measure, and designating two Council Members to prepare and submit a
  ballot argument in favor of the measure;
  2. Adopt Resolution No. 19-50 requesting the Board of Supervisors of the
  County of Los Angeles to consolidate, administer, manage and oversee the
  Election;
  3. Adopt Resolution No. 19-51 adopting regulations for candidates’
  statements; and
  4. Adopt Resolution No. 19-52, providing for rebuttal arguments relating to
  the ballot measure.

  B. MISSION DISTRICT ECONOMIC ANALYSIS AND MARKET STUDY
  PRESENTATION; RESOLUTION NO. 19-53 – AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR
  2019-20 OPERATING BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE $48,851 FOR THE
  REMAINING PORTION OF THE MISSION DISTRICT ECONOMIC ANALYSIS
  STUDY

  Earlier this year, the City entered into a professional services agreement with
  AECOM for a comprehensive economic analysis and market study of the
  Mission District. AECOM has conducted extensive research and site analysis and
  is prepared to present its findings to the City Council. The purpose of a
  comprehensive economic analysis and market study is to identify and evaluate

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 15, 2019  6
   current and future commercial development opportunities in order to help the
  City prioritize potential development opportunities in the Mission District.
  Potential developers interested in investing in the Mission District will benefit
  from the data as development scenarios derived from the study will provide
  valuable insight on whether a potential project will sustain future market
  conditions. Moreover, the City will benefit from knowing how to capitalize on
  the existing cultural assets such as the Mission Playhouse and San Gabriel
  Mission. The recommendations in the study shall serve to encourage new
  investment and help stimulate the area.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Receive and discuss the AECOM presentation on the Mission District
  Economic Analysis;
  2. Provide direction to staff, if necessary; and
  3. Adopt Resolution No. 19-53 amending the FY 2019-20 Operating Budget to
  appropriate $48,851 in the General Fund and Capital/Special Projects Fund
  for the Mission District Economic Analysis Study and amend the revenue
  estimate in the Capital/Special Projects Fund.

  C. FIRST READING OF AN ORDINANCE AMENDING TITLE III, SECTION 34 OF
  THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE – FINANCE AND REVENUE

  The proposed Ordinance will amend Title II, Section 34 of the San Gabriel
  Municipal Code by providing for the use of mechanical signatures on city issued
  checks, updating the purchasing procedures section to modify and clarify
  purchasing policies and procedures used to procure goods and services for City
  operations, and making minor modifications to the Informal Bidding
  Procedures for public projects. The majority of changes within the purchasing
  procedures code section were approved by Urgency Ordinance No. 656 on
  September 17, 2019 and are provided herein as to further ratify those
  provisions.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Ordinance No. 657 amending
  Title III, Section 34 of the San Gabriel Municipal Code, pertaining to Claims and
  Demands, Purchasing Procedures, and Informal Bidding Procedures.

  D. PRESENTATION ON THE METRO 710 FREEWAY MOBILITY IMPROVEMENT
  PROJECTS LIST

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 15, 2019  7
   Since 2017, Public Works staff have been working with the Los Angeles County
  Metropolitan Transportation Authority (Metro) to consider projects in cities
  affected by additional traffic created by the lack of a 710 Freeway connection
  between Interstate 10 in Alhambra and Interstate 210 in Pasadena. The Metro
  Board approved the first round of eligible mobility projects in November 2018,
  and approved the second round of eligible mobility improvement projects in
  September 2019. Metro is now ready to begin programming the approved
  projects and execute funding agreements with local agencies. Public Works
  staff submitted 24 potential projects, estimated at $144 million, to Metro for
  funding consideration including freeway interchange mobility and operation
  improvement projects, local street intersection improvement projects, and
  intelligent transportation systems (ITS) projects, Metro approved seven projects
  with a total estimated approved funding of $23 million.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff will present the City Council with an update on the Metro approved
  projects list for the SR-710 North Corridor Mobility Improvements.

 7. PUBLIC COMMENT

 8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

 9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

 10. CLOSED SESSION – None.

 11. ADJOURNMENT

  The next Regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, November 5, 2019
  at 6:30 p.m. in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San
  Gabriel, California. Information regarding matters to be considered at each
  meeting will be available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the
  City’s website at www.sangabrielcity.com.

  City Manager Lazzaretto explained that State Senator Rubio sponsored SB 751 which

I  housing projects. The COG has asked city managers and staff t o be part of a working
